content: To explore what happened with your Thunderbird installation we need several screen shots. Open Thunderbird, go to Help > Troubleshooting Information > Profile Folder > Open Folder..., then quit Thunderbird. in the profile folder xxxxxxxxx.default-release (or similar name) search for the prefs.js file and look up its size in kB. Also search for possible prefs-1.js (or in general prefs-x.js) files or an invalidprefs.js file and note creation date and size). Then go back in the folder hierarchy from the profile folder to its parent folder "Profiles" and take a screen shot of its contents. Thereafter go back one more step in the folder hierarchy and open the folder Thunderbird. It contains a file named profiles.ini: open this file with a simple text editor and make a screen shot of its contents.

content:
Hi Doug,

Do you mean the Cardbook add-on?

I installed it so I could try to help you.

It's supposed to collect addresses from the Thunderbird address books during installation. During my installation, it tried to do that and failed. Maybe it failed for you too and that is why you are asking.

I read that Cardbook can also import contacts. So one should be able to export an address book from Thunderbird in vcard format and import it into Cardbook. I exported an address book from Thunderbird, then could find no way in Cardbook to import it. If you are using the stand-alone app instead of the add-on, maybe you can find an import function there.

You could ask the developer for help: https://gitlab.com/CardBook/CardBook/-/work_items/574

Maybe someone else knows more.

content:
I can't fully explain it, but I bet it has something to do with the error message I get when I try to go to siteground.net with my web browser. See attached image. Apparently, the host has an invalid certificate, so Firefox blocks access. Perhaps Thunderbird does, too. The article cited in the error message also mentions that it could be due to your computer's anti-virus or security software.

Here's the text of the error message:

Be careful. Something doesn’t look right.

Firefox spotted a potentially serious security issue with siteground.net. Someone pretending to be the site could try to steal things like credit card info, passwords, or emails.

What makes the site look dangerous?

The site is set up to allow only secure connections, but there’s a problem with the site’s certificate. It’s possible that a bad actor is trying to impersonate the site. Sites use certificates issued by a certificate authority to prove they’re really who they say they are. Firefox doesn’t trust this site because its certificate isn’t valid for siteground.net. The certificate is only valid for: *.siteground.com, siteground.com.

What can you do about it?

Probably nothing, since it’s likely there’s a problem with the site itself. Sites use certificates issued by a certificate authority to prove they’re really who they say they are. But if you’re on a corporate network, your support team may have more info. If you’re using antivirus software, try searching for potential conflicts or known issues.

View the site’s certificate
